newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Arafat sees plot to "pulverise" peace process.
newsitem.headline: Arafat sees plot to "pulverise" peace process.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Tuesday accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of plotting to "pulverise" the Middle East peace process.
He told reporters after meeting Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali in Tunis:

"I have fully informed the president about the obstacles the Israeli prime minister is putting in the way of the peace process with the aim of freezing it. There is a plot to pulverise the peace process."
Arafat said he had thanked Ben Ali for Tunisia's support for the Palestinian and Jerusalem causes.

"Jerusalem is facing an Israeli attack to Judaise it. I appeal our Arab and Moslem nation to defend (East) Jerusalem because this is not only a Palestinian cause, but also an Arab, Moslem and Christian cause," he added.
Israeli-Palestinian peace moves ground to a halt in March after Israel starting building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

An official statement after the Arafat-Ben Ali meeting said Tunisia strongly condemned posters depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig which it said were pasted by "some Israeli extremist settlers" in the West Bank city of Hebron.
